eyebrow: CASS · The Haven interview day, Phoenix · 14 Oct 2026 · Traditional
title: Richard Southee, PhD:
title_short: Richard Southee, PhD · Three Times as Likely
headline: CASS found that a client with a case manager is almost three times as likely to have a positive outcome. There isn't one solution to homelessness; there are a thousand.
story: The finding: with a case manager, a client's odds of a positive outcome go up almost three times.
He writes policy thinking about the clients he worked with. All feedback is good, and if you want to complain, he's the guy to complain to.
Turn: not one solution to homelessness, but a thousand; every person needs a different one. Button: if clients know CASS cares and is working on it, CASS is doing a good job.
do: Open on the case-manager finding with the hook text on screen at 0:00.
Put the number on screen as he says <q>almost three times</q>.
Let the complaint line land with a smile.
Use the side angle (C4901) to hide the joins.
End on his face: <q>we're doing a good job.</q>
dont: Only the lines on this page; the transcript marks what is off limits.
No logo before the end card.

decisions.b: The brief says <q>Dr. Richard Southee · Former CEO, CASS</q>. cassaz.org (Our Leadership) lists <q>Richard Southee, PhD</q>, Director of Compliance and Continuous Improvement; on camera he calls himself the regional executive director and says he will not call himself a doctor. This plan uses the website's name and title. Nick confirms with Zsirai before export.

client_note: Why this matters: CASS wants supporters to see that the work is measured and human at the same time. A real finding, told warmly, does both.

[02:44.6] we're trying to accomplish with it.

[03:01.1] (line left out: not for this video)

[03:11.3] policies and procedures to make sure when we said we're going to do something that we're actually doing it.
[03:15.5] And then the other element of it is making sure that we're doing the things that no one is expecting us to do.
[03:21.7] But are needed in order to meet these goals.
[03:24.5] And so when someone says that they're expecting a certain level of outcomes, we have to actually be able to meet those outcomes.

[07:17.8] You know, I think
